:::{#def-pi}
#### The number $\pi$

The number $\pi \approx 3.14159$ is half of the circumference of the unit circle (@def-unit-circle).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-pi}
#### Distances around the unit circle

The whole unit circle has circumference $2\pi$.
Moving from $(1, 0)$ to $(-1, 0)$ along the upper half of the circle covers a distance of $\pi$,
and moving from $(1, 0)$ to $(0, 1)$ covers a quarter of the circle, a distance of $\pi/2$.

:::
